title: Case Workshop: Detecting and Responding
summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams identify terrorist and proliferation financing indicators, decide on screening, freezing and reporting, and agree control improvements.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams identify terrorist and proliferation financing indicators, decide on screening, freezing and reporting, and agree control improvements.
Learning Objectives: Apply typologies and red flags to a realistic multi-product case
Decide on freezing, reporting and relationship management
Agree an action plan to close gaps in the firm's framework
Syllabus: Case briefing: a payment and investment network with trade links
Freezing, reporting and the firm's response
Workshop: gap analysis and twelve-month action plan
Intended Audience: MLROs, compliance officers and financial crime analysts in investment, fund, payment, crypto-asset and fintech firms
Sanctions and screening teams responsible for customer, investor and payment screening
Senior managers and risk owners for products, corridors or customer segments with terrorist or proliferation financing exposure
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or sanctions screening is helpful. No prior specialist knowledge of terrorist or proliferation financing is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)
FATF, Best Practices on Combating the Abuse of Non-Profit Organisations (2023)
